title: Market Pulse
body_html:
This post reflects my current views on the market, sectors, and internal breadth/momentum. Expect candid, data-driven analysis, peppered with personal insights drawn from years of trading experience. I aim to provide value in every edition, helping you to see the market through a clearer, more informed lens.

What You Can Expect

  • In-Depth Market Analysis: A thorough examination of market trends, key indices, and pivotal turning points.

  • Sector Spotlights: A closer look at the hottest (and not-so-hot) sectors, highlighting opportunities and risks.

  • Breadth and Momentum Insights: Understanding the underlying strength of the market through breadth indicators and momentum metrics.

  • Themes and Setups: A look at the top stocks in terms of relative strength, momentum, trend, volatility, and liquidity to spot themes, setups, and opportunities

Exclusive Features

  • Interactive Spreadsheet: Alongside each post, I’ll link a detailed spreadsheet that tracks breadth and momentum metrics. This will allow you to follow along with the data and see the trends I’m analyzing day-by-day.

  • Quick Video Commentary: To complement the metrics, I’ll also be posting a quick video commentary several days a week. This will provide a more dynamic overview of the market, offering you additional context and clarity.

Market Metrics

Market Backdrop: Mixed

Markets continue to trade in a mixed fashion. Large caps attempted to break out on Thursday on the back of NVDA earnings, but Friday failed to deliver healthy follow-through. Still, the large-cap indices remain above their 10-day, 20-day, and 50-day moving averages. As long as they hold those technical lines in the sand, this early large-cap rally attempt still has a chance.

Mid- and small-cap indices did not fare as well. Not only did they fail to break out alongside large caps, but they also suffered sharp losses on Friday, pushing them back below key moving averages. This bifurcation between large caps and mid- and small-caps reinforces the mixed, sloppy nature of the current tape.

Sector strength continues to be led by Healthcare, Materials, Financials, Energy, and Technology from a relative strength and technical perspective. That said, even these leading areas are still working through pullbacks or consolidation and have not yet shown convincing upside follow-through. Consumer, Defensives, Industrials, Real Estate, and Utilities remain outright avoids for now due to weak relative strength and poor technical action.

Breadth and momentum remain mixed and soft as the market continues working through this corrective phase. The key is whether internals confirm the next move. If the indices break out to the upside, we want to see new highs and expanding upside momentum, while new lows and contracting downside momentum. If the market sees further corrective action, we want to see constructive divergence, meaning new lows and downside momentum remain contained rather than confirming the weakness.

Overall, this still looks like a constructive pullback within a larger uptrend, but buyers need to step up soon. The right approach is to stay selective, focus on the strongest groups, avoid weak sectors, and let breadth and momentum confirm whether the next move has real support underneath it.

Tactical Plan of Action

1) Trend & Market Structure

The market remains mixed and somewhat fragile. Large caps attempted to break out on the back of NVDA earnings, but Friday failed to deliver the kind of follow-through needed to confirm a stronger rally attempt. Still, large-cap indices remain above their 10-day, 20-day, and 50-day moving averages, which keeps their structure constructive for now.

Mid- and small-cap indices are the bigger concern. They failed to participate in the large-cap breakout attempt and then suffered sharp losses that pushed them back below key moving averages. That bifurcation reinforces the sloppy nature of the current tape.

Tactical guidance

  • Stay constructive, but do not get aggressive yet.

  • Keep exposure controlled until the market shows broader confirmation.

  • Favor large-cap leaders holding above key moving averages.

  • Be more cautious with mid- and small-cap exposure until those indices reclaim support.

  • Do not chase failed breakout attempts or weak follow-through.

  • If large caps hold their 10/20-day moving averages and begin pushing higher again, selectively add to quality setups.

  • If large caps lose the 20-day or mid/small caps continue deteriorating, shift more defensive.

2) Breadth & Momentum

Breadth and momentum remain mixed and soft. That means the market has not yet confirmed a broad-based upside move. The internals are not signaling full breakdown, but they are also not strong enough to support aggressive long exposure.

The next move needs confirmation. If the indices break higher, new highs and upside momentum should expand while new lows and downside momentum contract. Without that confirmation, any rally attempt remains suspect.

Tactical guidance

  • Use breadth and momentum as confirmation, not prediction.

  • Do not press aggressively until new highs expand and downside momentum contracts.

  • If breadth improves with price, begin adding selectively.

  • If the market rises but breadth remains soft, stay cautious.

  • If new lows expand meaningfully, tighten risk and reduce weaker positions.

  • Treat soft internals as a reason to be selective, not fully bearish.

3) Sector Focus & Rotation

Sector leadership remains concentrated but not fully convincing. Healthcare, Materials, Financials, Energy, and Technology continue to show the best combination of relative strength and technical structure. However, even these groups are mostly working through pullbacks or consolidations rather than showing strong upside follow-through.

Consumer, Defensives, Industrials, Real Estate, and Utilities remain avoids for now due to weak relative strength and poor technical action.

Tactical guidance

  • Keep Healthcare, Materials, Financials, Energy, and Technology as the main focus areas.

  • Prioritize only the cleanest setups within those groups.

  • Do not assume sector leadership is strong just because relative strength rankings look better.

  • Avoid Consumer, Defensives, Industrials, Real Estate, and Utilities until their structure improves.

  • Focus on groups that hold support and tighten constructively during the pullback.

4) Stock Selection & Entries

This is not a broad “buy everything” environment. The best opportunities should come from stocks in leading groups holding support, tightening near key moving averages, or preparing to break out from clean consolidation patterns.

Prioritize

  • Leaders in Healthcare, Materials, Financials, Energy, and Technology.

  • Stocks holding above rising 20-day and 50-day moving averages.

  • Tight bases and constructive pullbacks.

  • Names showing relative strength while the broader market chops.

  • Stocks reclaiming the 10-day and 20-day with volume support.

  • Breakouts only if breadth and market structure confirm.

Avoid

  • Mid- and small-cap names breaking support.

  • Stocks in weak sectors with poor relative strength.

  • Loose, wide, volatile patterns.

  • Failed breakouts that fall back into prior ranges.

  • Buying names simply because they are down.

  • Breakouts without follow-through from the broader market.

5) Trade Management & Risk Controls

The current tape requires discipline. Large caps still have constructive structure, but weak follow-through, soft internals, and mid- and small-cap weakness mean risk should be managed carefully.

Risk controls

  • Use smaller initial entries until confirmation improves.

  • Add only if the trade starts working and the market supports the move.

  • Keep stops tight on names losing the 20-day moving average.

  • Cut failed breakouts quickly.

  • Take partial profits into sharp strength if the tape remains choppy.

  • Do not average down into weak charts.

  • Hold only stocks showing relative strength, clean structure, and support at key levels.

6) Scenario Plan

Current Case: Mixed Corrective Pullback

Large caps remain above key moving averages, but mid/small caps are weak and breadth remains soft.

Action: Stay involved, but selective. Focus only on the strongest groups and avoid adding aggressively.

Bullish Confirmation Scenario

This develops if large caps add to breakout gains, mid/small caps reclaim key moving averages, and breadth/momentum expand to the upside.

Action: Add exposure through clean setups in Healthcare, Materials, Financials, Energy, and Technology.

Large-Cap Only Scenario

This develops if SPY and QQQ hold up, but mid/small caps continue to lag.

Action: Stay focused on large-cap leaders only. Avoid weaker, lower-quality areas of the market.

Continued Chop Scenario

This develops if indices remain stuck near current levels and internals stay mixed.

Action: Trade smaller, reduce trade count, and wait for cleaner setups.

Defensive Shift Scenario

This develops if large caps lose the 20-day, mid/small caps weaken further, and new lows expand.

Action: Tighten stops, raise cash, and stop buying breakouts until the market stabilizes.

Bottom Line

The market remains in a constructive pullback, but the tape is not clean. Large caps are still holding key moving averages and have a chance to resume higher, but the lack of follow-through after the NVDA-driven breakout attempt and the weakness in mid- and small-caps argue for caution.

The right posture is selective and patient. Focus on Healthcare, Materials, Financials, Energy, and Technology, avoid weak sectors, and wait for breadth and momentum to confirm the next move before pressing harder.
